decisions.id: B5-no-pair
decisions.summary: Bookends row 5: no timing pair at batch 5's (wave 106's) close because its engine code is off the pair's path
decisions.why: Carried from wave 106's round 4 (CLEAR); plan.md's text for it is unchanged by HEAD~1, which only appends the Wave 107 section. Narrows FR-003's literal 'one timing pair and its perf-audit', exactly as B4-no-pair did, and B4's stated condition (holds only while a batch's engine code stays off the hamlet roll path) is re-measured here, not carried over. The batch's engine delta (git diff de5f96acb..HEAD on l7r/pool): compound_model.py, compound_parts.py, pack_audit (__init__, checks, registry), buildings/types.json (the tubs_off_their_doors check name added to two types' check lists), and four modal .md files; no pool gen or pool json. Measured: importing exactly what perf_snapshot imports (hamletgen, hamletgen.driver, hamletgen.plan, settlement, _invocation, tools.perf_bands) loads 247 l7r modules, none of compound, compound_model, compound_parts, pack_audit or buildings.*; the one name-alike, settlement.structures.compounds, imports only _geom and _knobs; no file under hamletgen/ or settlement/ reads types.json, DOOR_KINDS or TUB_DOOR_MAX_FT; _invocation names compound and pack_audit only as strings in a table. So the pair would time byte-identical code and could detect nothing this batch did - the rule's purpose cannot be served, and a band-3 noise reading would send the GM a sign-off on nothing. The gate premise also checks: .git/verification-state.json records make done green-local at 7817f4a30, engine key 4ade95493877..., the current key, and HEAD changes no engine path after it. Residue (not a ruling): the row's list of the batch's engine code omits buildings/types.json, which batch 4's row named; add it so the row states the whole delta it rests on.

decisions.id: W107-c the hill shrine's burial ground claimed UNRESEARCHED
decisions.summary: the table's rule that a village whose shrine stands on a hill keeps its burial ground apart is claimed 'UNRESEARCHED: no source says whether graves climbed a hill shrine's slope'
decisions.why: The premise is not measured against the record. research/questions/0236-where-a-village-buries-its-dead-its-own-ground-the-temple-yard-the-fields-or-the-home-plot.drawing.html records this exact rule ('Our maps never put a village's graves at a shrine on a hill ... a village whose shrine stands on a hill always takes a ground apart'), with a source-backed survey of two-grave villages pointing the same way, and labels it 'a GUESS: no source we read says so outright'. 328's ranking applies one convention throughout (row 4: 'the claim should read GUESS 0222.drawing'; row 20: 'GUESS on 0105's drawing page'; row 16: 'UNRESEARCHED, or the guess recorded on that page'): UNRESEARCHED is for a rule no page carries, and where a drawing page records the guess the claim is GUESS <that page>. Claiming UNRESEARCHED here detaches the implementation from the research it has. That is a mislabel, and 328 FR-004 says an E0 fix exists to correct mislabels. The claim should read: <!-- Research: a hill shrine's village keeps its burial ground apart - GUESS research/questions/0236-where-a-village-buries-its-dead-its-own-ground-the-temple-yard-the-fields-or-the-home-plot.drawing.html: a village whose shrine stands on a hill takes a ground apart; no source says so outright -->, and the plan's Wave 107 bullet should say the same. Note: the ranking's own fix ('citing ... 0226') was also wrong, since 0226 says nothing about a hill shrine. Do not fall back to it. An impl-drift IN-STEP on the UNRESEARCHED label does not settle this: the request is that the implementation match the research it has, which is a different test from whether a checker accepts a label.
